questions.question: What is the primary goal of informal-to-formal translation (autoformalization) in the context of theorem proving?
questions.choice_A: To convert natural-language mathematical statements into machine-checkable formal specifications and proofs
questions.choice_B: To generate human-readable summaries of formal proofs
questions.choice_C: To reduce the computational complexity of proof search algorithms
questions.choice_D: To replace interactive theorem provers with fully autonomous systems

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a key challenge in autoformalization of informal mathematics?
questions.choice_A: Excessive reliance on symbolic computation libraries
questions.choice_B: Bridging underspecified, context-dependent language with precise formal semantics
questions.choice_C: Lack of standardized file formats for proofs
questions.choice_D: The need to manually optimize SAT solver heuristics

questions.question: Which description best distinguishes Coq from Isabelle/HOL and Lean?
questions.choice_A: Coq is based on higher-order logic without dependent types
questions.choice_B: Coq uses a resolution-based proof search engine by default
questions.choice_C: Coq is built on the Calculus of Inductive Constructions with dependent types and proof terms
questions.choice_D: Coq emphasizes classical set theory as its foundation

questions.question: What is Sledgehammer in the Isabelle ecosystem?
questions.choice_A: A proof kernel that checks all proof terms
questions.choice_B: A tactic for rewriting terms into normal form
questions.choice_C: A module for extracting code to functional languages
questions.choice_D: A bridge that calls external automated provers and reconstructs proofs in Isabelle

questions.question: Which comparison between Isabelle, Coq, and Lean is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Isabelle/HOL emphasizes classical higher-order logic; Coq focuses on constructive dependent type theory; Lean supports dependent type theory with a growing mathematical library (mathlib).
questions.choice_B: All three rely exclusively on first-order logic foundations.
questions.choice_C: Lean lacks automation support while Isabelle is purely manual.
questions.choice_D: Coq and Lean do not support tactic-based proof development.

questions.question: In evaluation pipelines, why is the proof assistant’s kernel considered part of the trusted computing base (TCB)?
questions.choice_A: Because it automatically generates lemmas during proof search
questions.choice_B: Because it verifies that every accepted proof follows from the axioms and inference rules
questions.choice_C: Because it translates proofs into multiple logics for cross-checking
questions.choice_D: Because it guarantees minimal proof length

questions.question: What characterizes a proof sketch compared to a full formal proof?
questions.choice_A: A proof sketch contains explicit proof terms and passes the kernel
questions.choice_B: A proof sketch is a sequence of SAT solver calls
questions.choice_C: A proof sketch outlines the high-level reasoning steps without fully elaborated, machine-checkable details
questions.choice_D: A proof sketch is only valid for propositional logic

questions.question: Which statement about automated provers used alongside proof assistants is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: They eliminate the need for tactics in interactive environments.
questions.choice_B: They can only handle quantifier-free arithmetic problems.
questions.choice_C: They require the proof assistant to be based on set theory.
questions.choice_D: They often work as external oracles (e.g., E, Vampire, Z3) whose results are reconstructed or rechecked in the assistant.

questions.question: What is a typical evaluation metric for autoformalization systems producing proofs in assistants like Lean or Isabelle?
questions.choice_A: Solve rate under time and resource limits, verified by the proof assistant’s kernel
questions.choice_B: Average number of tokens generated by the language model
questions.choice_C: Number of informal examples paraphrased per minute
questions.choice_D: The ratio of symbolic to numeric tokens in the prompt

questions.question: Which best describes the miniF2F benchmark?
questions.choice_A: A dataset of industrial verification problems for model checkers
questions.choice_B: A suite of formalized competition-style math problems used to evaluate theorem proving and autoformalization, often in Lean and Isabelle
questions.choice_C: A benchmark for code synthesis from formal specifications
questions.choice_D: A benchmark exclusively measuring proof length minimization

questions.question: Why is proof reconstruction important after calling an external automated prover?
questions.choice_A: To compress the proof to its shortest form
questions.choice_B: To avoid depending on the external prover’s correctness by re-deriving the result within the assistant’s logic
questions.choice_C: To convert the proof into a probabilistic certificate
questions.choice_D: To ensure the proof is compatible with multiple programming languages

questions.question: In the context of verification pipelines, what role does elaboration play in systems like Lean?
questions.choice_A: It enumerates all possible tactics from a given state
questions.choice_B: It transforms informal English into formal terms
questions.choice_C: It resolves implicit arguments, infers types, and constructs proof terms from tactic scripts
questions.choice_D: It converts proofs into SAT instances for external solvers

questions.question: Which limitation commonly affects current autoformalization approaches?
questions.choice_A: They cannot parse LaTeX or MathML
questions.choice_B: They often hallucinate definitions or lemmas not present in the target library, leading to non-checking proofs
questions.choice_C: They only work for propositional logic and fail on arithmetic
questions.choice_D: They require theorem provers to be non-interactive

questions.question: Which statement about tactic-based proof development is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Tactics replace the kernel in checking correctness.
questions.choice_B: Tactics script interactive steps; the kernel still validates the resulting proof objects or derivations.
questions.choice_C: Tactics are incompatible with dependent type theories.
questions.choice_D: Tactics guarantee shortest proofs by design.

questions.question: What is a risk when evaluating informal-to-formal systems on benchmarks like miniF2F?
questions.choice_A: Benchmarks forbid the use of any automation
questions.choice_B: External provers cannot be integrated during evaluation
questions.choice_C: Data leakage or memorization from training corpora can inflate measured performance
questions.choice_D: All problems are trivial for symbolic methods

questions.question: Why might two autoformalization systems produce different but both valid formalizations of the same informal statement?
questions.choice_A: Only one of them can use classical logic
questions.choice_B: Formal libraries differ in canonical definitions, and multiple equivalent formal encodings may exist
questions.choice_C: Dependent types forbid multiple encodings of the same concept
questions.choice_D: The kernel enforces a unique proof term for each theorem

questions.question: Which architectural distinction is characteristic of the LCF-style approach used by systems like Isabelle and HOL family provers?
questions.choice_A: A small trusted kernel enforces soundness; higher-level automation builds on top via derived inference rules
questions.choice_B: A large trusted automation layer with an untrusted kernel
questions.choice_C: No separation between proof search and proof checking
questions.choice_D: Proofs are accepted based solely on external certificates without checking

questions.question: In a typical evaluation pipeline for automated theorem proving with large language models, what is a standard protocol to ensure reliability?
questions.choice_A: Accept any proof that appears syntactically correct
questions.choice_B: Require the generated proof to be checked by the proof assistant within time limits and report success@k over multiple samples
questions.choice_C: Ignore kernel errors if external provers claim success
questions.choice_D: Score models by BLEU overlap with ground-truth proof scripts

questions.question: How does Lean’s mathlib influence evaluation and development of autoformalization methods?
questions.choice_A: It prevents the use of classical axioms in all proofs
questions.choice_B: It provides a large, standardized library of definitions and lemmas that systems can target for reuse and grounding
questions.choice_C: It disables tactic-based proofs to encourage declarative styles
questions.choice_D: It requires all proofs to be externally reconstructed

questions.question: Which of the following best captures the semantic gap autoformalization must bridge?
questions.choice_A: Translating numerical constants into strings
questions.choice_B: Mapping informal, context-rich mathematical discourse into precise formal syntax and proof obligations compatible with a specific library and logic
questions.choice_C: Converting proofs into images for visualization
questions.choice_D: Replacing dependencies with randomized lemmas to test robustness
